newsitem.title: PERU: Peruvian rebel leaves site of hostage talks.
newsitem.headline: Peruvian rebel leaves site of hostage talks.

text.p: A second round of direct talks between the government and Marxist rebels holding 72 captives ended after about three hours on Friday.

A white Red Cross car that had ferried a Tupac Amaru Revolutionary Movement (MRTA) guerrilla to a safe house for the talks to end the 59-day hostage crisis was seen travelling back to the besieged Japanese ambassador's home where the rebels are holed up.
Two mediators in the talks, Roman Catholic Bishop Juan Luis Cipriani and Red Cross representative Michel Minnig, also left the house across from the diplomatic compound being used for the talks.
Friday's meeting was the second since Tuesday, when the two sides broke a deadlock by meeting face-to-face for the first time since Dec. 28.
Rebels have held the hostages since Dec. 17, when they stormed a cocktail party and seized hundreds of guests.
They have since released most of the captives. Those remaining include the ambassadors of Japan and Bolivia and President Alberto Fujimori's brother Pedro.
